crime: Before prison, a friend kept leaving their games early, promising a next time. Then she stopped coming.

The first time the girl and {WITCH_NAME} swam in the lake, the girl splashed her, and they laughed together. Today, {WITCH_NAME} divided into two bodies and kept up a noisy volley of splashes around the girl.
The girl signaled to a prisoner for a towel, then began swimming toward shore before their next race, leaving the game unfinished. Before she reached shore, {WITCH_NAME} called, “Goodbye.”

Beneath the water, one of {WITCH_NAME}’s bodies seized the girl’s ankles and held her down until she drowned. At the same time, the other body stayed at the surface, gripped the girl’s wrists, and hauled upward as if trying to save her. Then the two bodies met beneath the surface, embraced, and reunited, leaving one apparent rescuer.

After the girl’s body was recovered, a prisoner believed the rescue had simply failed. Examining the girl’s ankles, the prisoner found finger-shaped bruises encircling them. The prisoner remembered that throughout the struggle, both of {WITCH_NAME}’s visible hands had kept their grip on the girl’s wrists. The prisoners matched the bruises to that memory and exposed the trick: her divided selves had held the girl in opposing grips.
fields.epitaph: No number of selves could replace the girl who laughed with her.
execution: The execution stand locks the witch upright, her torso against the backplate of a drum-shaped frame. Mechanical mallets begin drumming on her chest. They beat faster and faster, never breaking rhythm even after her body goes slack.

magic.name: One Mind, Many Bodies
magic.text: She can divide herself into multiple bodies that act independently while sharing a single consciousness.
